title: Microsoft confirms authentication failures with some third-party apps and devices after NTLM signing changes in November updates
summary: Microsoft's support page KB5135557 says authentication through some third-party apps and devices, including authentication proxies, SSO solutions and application packaging tools that use NTLM, fails after the November 2026 update or a later update with the new NTLM signing changes. Microsoft says the cause is a device that sends an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field, and gives a temporary registry workaround. BleepingComputer reported on 25 November that no fix was available yet.
plain: Microsoft says some third-party apps and devices that use NTLM can fail to sign in after the November 2026 Windows update. It offers a temporary registry workaround.
exec: Microsoft confirms the November NTLM signing changes can break sign-ins for some third-party apps and devices.
action: Microsoft advises checking whether the device or app supports Kerberos or has a vendor update meeting the new NTLM requirements; as a temporary measure it describes setting ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm to 1 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0.
